description:
A desktop viewer and source-level editor for hierarchical data files — XML, JSON, TOML and CSV.

Klados shows a data file three ways, kept in sync: its structure as a tree, the selected node's contents as tables, and the source text exactly as it is on disk.
Repeating children become a grid you can sort, filter and export. Editing happens in the source, and saving writes the file byte for byte, in its original encoding.
- Regex search can't freeze Klados any more. Regex Find runs in the background, so the window stays responsive. A pattern that takes more than 2 seconds on one part of the file stops, keeps the matches found so far, and says "(stopped)".
- Case-insensitive search follows Unicode, in plain and regex mode alike.
- Invalid regex patterns say so. Find shows "Invalid pattern" with the reason, instead of "No matches".
- Copy path works in every format. Pasted into the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), the copied path finds its node in JSON, TOML and CSV too, not only in XML. Names with spaces or special characters are quoted, as in "first name".
- Safer saving. Save checks for free space first, so a full disk leaves your file untouched instead of half-written. The file is updated in place, so its owner, permissions, hidden attribute and links stay as they were. Hidden files on Windows can now be saved.
- Reloading never loses edits. Edits made while a reload is running are kept, and Klados asks what to do.
- Markdown export escapes backslashes and line breaks in cells, so the table no longer breaks.
- Security hardening. The installed app can no longer be used to run other code, and it checks its own files at startup. Klados installed in a folder whose path contains ~, [, ] or % now works. Every release file is listed in SHA256SUMS.txt.
